raw_record.question_text:
As shown in the figure, an object with mass $m=1\mathrm{kg}$ is placed on a horizontal surface. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the surface is $\mu=0.3$. The object starts from rest and undergoes uniformly accelerated motion under the action of a constant horizontal force $F=6\mathrm{N}$. $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. The magnitude of the acceleration $a$ of an object with uniform acceleration.
2. When its speed reaches $12\mathrm{m/s}$, the distance $x$ traveled by the object
3. If the force $F$ is removed at the end of 4 seconds, how much farther can the object move?

method.method_draft: First read the image as a block on a horizontal rough surface with an applied horizontal force F pointing to the right, so the normal force is vertical and friction opposes the rightward motion. From the text take m=1 kg, μ=0.3, F=6 N, g=10 m/s^2, initial rest, target speed 12 m/s, and force removal at t=4 s. Use N=mg=10 N and kinetic friction f_k=μN=3 N, so while F acts the net horizontal force is 6−3=3 N and a=F_net/m=3 m/s^2. For part 2 use constant-acceleration kinematics from rest: v^2=2ax, so x=12^2/(2·3)=24 m. For part 3 find the speed at 4 s: v=at=3·4=12 m/s. After F is removed, only kinetic friction acts, giving deceleration μg=3 m/s^2; the stopping distance is v^2/(2μg)=12^2/(2·3)=24 m.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：附图显示一个方块状物体放在水平粗糙面上，表面用斜线表示粗糙水平地面；物体左侧有一个标为 F 的水平箭头指向右方，表示外力 F 向右作用在物体上。因此支持力竖直向上，重力竖直向下，摩擦力与向右运动趋势相反、向左。

推理：已知 m=1 kg，μ=0.3，F=6 N，g=10 m/s^2，物体从静止开始。水平面上 N=mg=1×10=10 N，所以动摩擦力 f_k=μN=0.3×10=3 N。外力作用时，水平合力 F_net=6−3=3 N，因此加速度 a=F_net/m=3/1=3 m/s^2。

当速度达到 12 m/s 时，由从静止开始的匀加速公式 v^2=2ax，得 x=12^2/(2×3)=144/6=24 m。

力 F 作用 4 s 后，速度 v=at=3×4=12 m/s。撤去 F 后，只受摩擦力减速，减速度大小为 μg=0.3×10=3 m/s^2。停止距离 s=v^2/(2μg)=12^2/(2×3)=144/6=24 m。

1. a = 3 m/s^2
2. x = 24 m
3. farther distance = 24 m

Reasoning: It is known that m=1 kg, μ=0.3, F=6 N, g=10 m/s^2, and the object starts from rest. On the horizontal surface N=mg=1×10=10 N, so the kinetic friction force f_k=μN=0.3×10=3 N. When the external force acts, the horizontal resultant force F_net=6−3=3 N, therefore the acceleration a=F_net/m=3/1=3 m/s^2.

When the velocity reaches 12 m/s, from the uniformly accelerated motion formula starting from rest v^2=2ax, obtain x=12^2/(2×3)=144/6=24 m.

After force F acts for 4 s, the velocity v=at=3×4=12 m/s. After F is removed, only friction acts to decelerate it, and the magnitude of the deceleration is μg=0.3×10=3 m/s^2. The stopping distance s=v^2/(2μg)=12^2/(2×3)=144/6=24 m.
